title: War of Love
text:
The time that silvers my beard

hollowed my eyes and enlarged my forehead,

is becoming transparent memory in me,

and the deeper the bottom, the clearer it grows.


Childhood fear, adolescent love,

how this autumn light beautifies you!

sour roads of ugly life,

you too are gilded in the setting sun!


How in the fountain where the water dwells

an inscription stands out in stone:

the abacus of time lacks one hour!


And how that absence at a rendezvous,

beneath the elms that November gilds,

rises from the depths of my history!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Machado's autumnal recollection and the missing hour on time's abacus.

title: As on the High Plain Your Figure
text:
How on the high plain your figure

appears to me!... My word evokes

the green meadow and the arid plain,

the flowering bramble, the ashen rock.


And obedient memory, a black holm oak

sprouts on the hill, the poplar descends to the river;

the shepherd climbs up to the hill;

a balcony of the city shines: mine,


ours. Do you see? Toward Aragon, far off,

the Moncayo range, white and rose...

Look at the blaze of that crimson cloud,


and that star in the blue, wife.

Beyond the Duero, the hill of Santana

turns purple in the silent afternoon.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the landscape summoned by memory and the intimate turn from mine to ours.

title: Childhood Memory
text:
A brown and cold afternoon

of winter. The schoolboys

study.

Monotony

of rain behind the windowpanes.


It is the classroom. On a poster

Cain is shown

fugitive, and

Abel dead,

beside a crimson stain.


With sonorous hollow timbre

the teacher thunders, an old man

badly

dressed, lean and dry,

holding a book in his hand.


And an entire children's choir

goes singing the lesson:

"a thousand times

one hundred, one hundred thousand;

a thousand times a thousand, a million."


A brown and cold afternoon

of winter. The schoolboys

study.

Monotony

of rain behind the windowpanes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the rainy classroom monotony and the mechanical multiplication chant.

title: To the Great Zero
text:
When the Being that one is made nothingness

and rested, which it well deserved,

the day already had night, and company

man had in the absence of the beloved.


Fiat threshold. Human thought sprang up.

and the universal egg lifted, empty,

now without color, desubstantiated and cold,

full of weightless fog, in its hand.


Take the integral zero, the hollow sphere,

which you must look at upright, if you are to see it.

Today that the back of your beast is a back,


and the miracle of non-being is fulfilled,

offer, poet, a border song

to death, to silence and to oblivion.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the philosophical strangeness of Machado's address to zero and non-being.

title: The Sad Sea
text:
A sea of steel with gray waves throbs

inside the rough gnawed walls

of the old port. The north wind blows

and ruffles the sea. The sad sea lulls

a bitter illusion with its gray waves.

The north wind ruffles the sea, and the sea lashes

the harbor wall.

The afternoon closes the horizon

clouded over. Above the steel sea

there is a leaden sky.

The red brigantine is a bloody

phantom, over the sea, which the sea shakes...

Gloomily the north wind hums and whistles sadly

on the harsh lyre of the sturdy rigging.

The red brigantine is a phantom

that the wind agitates and the ruffled sea rocks,

the rough ruffled sea of gray waves.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the metallic sea, red brigantine, and rigging as a harsh lyre.

title: Yesterday My Sorrows Were...
text:
Yesterday my sorrows were

like silkworms

that went crafting cocoons;

today they are black butterflies.


From how many bitter flowers

I drew white wax!

Oh time when my griefs

worked like bees!


Today they are like wild oats,

or darnel in a sown field,

like blight in the ear,

like woodworm in wood.


Oh time when my sorrows

had good tears,

and were like water from a waterwheel

that goes irrigating an orchard!

Today they are torrent water

that tears the silt from the earth.


Sorrows that yesterday made

my heart a beehive,

today treat my heart

like an old wall:

they want to tear it down, and soon,

with the blows of the pickaxe.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the transformation of grief from bees and irrigation into torrent and demolition.

title: You Know It, Beloved
text:
...


now we can

make our impossible

dreams come true

that honeymoon in an exotic sky

all-inclusive trip


sea views intimate

twilights reviewed by experts

within our

reach all

the romantic silences

with the new system of

comfortable

installment payments: to choose

privileged islands or places


of high society—that dream

is now a reality—

(or else stay

here beside the breach

next to the struggle, for there is still time

to risk

one's hide for something)

one of two, my beloved, do not forget


that choosing is the only problem

this system offers.


"Domestic Fables" 1972
editorial_note: The translation keeps the consumer-parody voice and the choice between packaged romance and risky struggle.

title: The Star Wept Pink...
text:
The star wept pink, caught on your ear,

infinity, white, rolled over your shoulders,

the sea iridesced red-haired over your breasts

and man bled black along your goddess flank.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the color sequence and the compressed visionary anatomy.
